author: reek
body: An effect operation that no handler ever gives a value is not zero.

author: reek
body: The handler table has one slot per declared operation, and a slot is only ever written by a handler clause. An operation that TAKES ARGUMENTS is emitted as a call, so a missing implementation is caught at the call fixup: CDX2040. A NULLARY one is emitted as a load from its slot, and no fixup ever sees a load. Every nullary operation with no handler therefore read a slot nobody had written -- zeroed memory -- and the read yielded zero. Zero is a plausible Integer, an empty Text and an empty List all at once, so nothing downstream could tell it apart from an answer.

author: reek
body: thread-idx-x is the one that shows what that is worth. Compiled for the PTX or SPIR-V plug it lowers to the real grid index. Compiled for x86, where there is no grid, it read zero and said nothing -- so a kernel built for the host by mistake became thread 0 of block 0, computed one lane of the work, and exited successfully.

author: reek
body: The same silence once covered current-user and authenticate, the identity primitives, until they were given definitions over the identity builtins (Foreword chapter Identity) and became performable. gpu-init is still unhandled, and thread-idx-x below is the one this test drives.

author: reek
body: CDX2034. The arity of an operation no longer decides whether the compiler tells you it has no implementation.
